question: Does the official UPLB thesis catalog provide the full Orozco estero study or resolve whether the 2008 article and 2012 chapter are independent field surveys?

catalogFinding.repository: University Knowledge Digital Repository, University of the Philippines Los Baños
catalogFinding.title: Biophysico-chemical and socioeconomic study of two major Manila esteros
catalogFinding.author: Glorina D. Perez-Orozco
catalogFinding.degree: Master of Science in Environmental Science
catalogFinding.fullTextAvailability: The repository record states that the document is currently not available there.

crossRecordComparison.dlsu2008Record: The DLSU Animo Repository abstract says the fish survey was part of the senior author's dissertation for a Ph.D. in Environmental Science, but its upload is unavailable.
crossRecordComparison.degreeConflict: The UPLB catalog lists an MS in Environmental Science while the DLSU abstract says Ph.D. Environmental Science. The available records do not explain this difference; preserve it as unresolved metadata rather than correcting either source.
crossRecordComparison.2012Chapter: The Springer abstract names the same two esteros and the same four fish taxa as the 2008 abstract, but full chapter access is subscription-only. The accessible material cannot establish whether the chapter reports new sampling or republishes the thesis/article dataset.
crossRecordComparison.lineageDecision: The catalog strengthens the link between the research topic and a 2008 UPLB graduate thesis, but does not resolve whether the 2008 article and 2012 chapter are independent datasets.

evidenceLimits.stationData: No accessible thesis file or fish-by-station table was found in the official catalog record.
evidenceLimits.sampleProvenance: No voucher identifiers, station-linked accession records, coordinates, collection dates, or fish effort details are supplied by the catalog metadata.
evidenceLimits.reuse: This review uses bibliographic metadata only. No thesis text, figures, tables, or fish records are reproduced.

evidenceDecision.decision: Add the UPLB record as a bibliographic source only. Keep the study lineage, degree discrepancy, species-to-station assignments, and dataset overlap unresolved.

nextActions: If an authorized full thesis copy or author-provided manuscript becomes available, compare its fish methods, station map, species tables, collection dates, and voucher records with both abstracts before assessing dataset overlap.

Until then, retain the four fish names only as an aggregated historical research lead for Estero de San Miguel and Estero de Quiapo; do not transfer them to Pasig River or claim station-specific occurrence.
